subject: dwarfRifleman
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf rifleman with braided beard and blunderbuss.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm reviewing the render against the character's key identity traits—the braided beard and helmet with goggles look solid, but the blunderbuss reads awkwardly, pointing up with its bell facing the wrong way so it resembles a horn more than a gun. The dwarf's proportions also seem off, with legs too long for the stocky build the character should have.

The head looks too small and sunken into the pauldrons, making the eyes nearly invisible, so I want to enlarge and reposition the eye decals to make them more prominent against the oversized red nose and cheeks. I'm also checking the lowest points of the model—base cylinder, iron sole, and rocks—to make sure nothing clips below the ground plane, adjusting the rock placement height so the bottoms stay within acceptable tolerance. Finally I'm working out the gun's grip and orientation in model space to figure out why the bell appears to point the wrong direction in the three-quarter view.

Checking the reach, the left hand is too far from the shoulder to support the barrel at that position, so the dwarf's left arm hanging naturally might be the simpler fix, or I could shift the gun's position closer to center to make the grip reachable.

Given limited time, I'm prioritizing the fixes that matter most: making the eyes bigger, fixing the lowest point of the model, resolving floating geometry pieces, cleaning up the gun's silhouette, and adjusting head scale. I also notice the back tabard panel is floating slightly off the hips geometry and needs to shift closer to the body to avoid a visible gap.

The tabard top should sit near the belly's edge and hang down over the thighs, which seems fine to leave as-is in front. For the back piece, I'm considering nudging the z-position slightly closer in, around -0.145, since the current gap looks a bit loose.

The beard gem placement looks fine to leave alone. For head sizing, I'm weighing whether to enlarge the skull blob versus just refining the eyes and brow area, since brow position at that height seems to be covering the eyes currently.

Let me enlarge the eyes and reposition them with a higher elevation, then raise the brow blobs so they don't overlap. I also want to shrink the oversized nose ball and tone down the cheek color slightly.

Checking the back view, the bedroll and powder horn look fine as is. For the trumpet's bell, the current elevation makes it tower near head height like a trumpet beside the face — I should lower it so the bell sits closer to chest level instead.

I'm checking whether the stock position intersects with the forearm, since the elbow bends backward there; it seems moderately safe at the current angle, so I'll settle on orientation vector (0, 0.5, 0.87) and work out the matching up-vector through a cross product with the side axis.

I should also update the hard-coded wood grain axis to match this new orientation, and I'm noticing a leftover degenerate zero-radius sphere in the glow code that I should just remove rather than keep as dead geometry.

Replacing with a cleaner shell stick, slightly enlarging the bandolier shells for visibility, and leaving the helmet crest and skull scale as they are for now.

Now I'm adjusting precise facial proportions: raising the rock position height, tweaking eye placement and size, nudging the brow blob y-coordinates up slightly for both sides, and shrinking the nose and cheek blob sizes for a subtler look. Each edit targets a unique matching line in the source.

Next I'm defining the gun's forward direction vector and the wood grip's axis orientation.
